catalog_quote: 1.3 Tone There are two lexical tones in Gude: level high tone, and level low tone. These tones on the syllable serve to distinguish vocabulary items, but do not serve to distinguish the grammatical categories of the language. Tone sandhi phenomena have not been sufficiently investigated, and hence are not discussed in this grammar. Tone marking occurs on most main entries in the dictionary, but is only rarely indicated in the grammar. High tone is indicated by acute accent " ´ " and low tone is indicated by grave accent " ` ". Examples: /àyə̀wá/ ayuwa grasshopper /áyə́wà/ ayuwa name of a town /sʸə̀wá/ shiwa stirring stick /sʸə́wà/ shiwa come (imperative sing.) /bá'à/ ba'a and /bà'á/ ba'a back /ɬá:ɬà/ lhaalha cattle egret /ɬá:ɬá/ lhaalha prickly fuzz (on plants)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Gude is not in the catalog. The single title-hit, Hoskison 1974 'Prosodies and verb stems in Gude' (Linguistics 141: 17-26), is a De Gruyter paywalled article with no open copy anywhere (Crossref/Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex/Unpaywall all closed; De Gruyter served a bot-check stub; SIL archive 403). Independent second-hand descriptions read in this search of works with stress in the title (Gravina 2014 LOT 375 pp. 75-76 and its summary of Schuh 2002; Hoskison's own 1975 thesis and 1983 dissertation) show 'prosodies' means Firthian palatalization/labialization spreading on verb roots, not stress or accent, so the item is prosody-but-not-word-stress and low priority. The full first-hand Gude sources already held by the project (Hoskison 1975 MA, Hoskison 1983 grammar-dictionary, Anderson & Menetrey 1990 tone study, Menetrey & Perrin 2006 orthography) describe a two-tone (H/L) system and contain no statement on word stress. No first-hand stress statement for Gude was found; the best new statement = none. Records saved and logged in

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gude is described as a two-tone language (level H vs level L, lexically contrastive, no grammatical tone reported). The grammar's phonology chapter (consonants, vowels, tone, orthography, consonant length) contains no statement at all about word stress or accent placement; neither does the author's 1975 MA phonology. So: tonal, source silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tone: dictionary intro notes final-syllable tone often unmarked because underlying final high vowels are devoiced/deleted before pause; tone sandhi uninvestigated.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern lexical items/citation forms; pre-pausal (citation-form) vowel lengthening of final /a/ and deletion of final high vowel are described (pp. 16-17) but not linked to stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Hoskison's data (1975, 1983) come from speakers of Lamurde (Nwuvi) village, Nigerian side (Mubi area, Adamawa State); he states Gude 'is a single dialect', mutually intelligible with Fali of Vimtim and Fali of Bahuli (the 'Fali of Mubi' cluster). Matches gude1246 at language level; the SIL Cameroon items (Anderson 1990, Menetrey & Perrin 2006) describe the Cameroonian (Boukoula area) variety of the same language.

new_statements.quote: TON ... Le ton est lexical, mais jusqu'ici quelques paires minimales seulement ont été trouvées. Aucun rôle grammatical du ton n'a été trouvé. L'absence des marques de ton ne pose pas de problèmes pour la lecture, sauf dans le cas des deux mots ma, voir 2.4 a) consonnes géminées et la note 2. [fn. 2, p. 7, decoded from the custom font:] La combinaison de ces deux morphèmes dans l'orthographe est une convention pour distinguer le ma 'conditionel' (ton bas) du ma 'marquer du topique' (ton haut) sans introduire les accents dans l'orthographe.
new_statements.translation: TONE ... Tone is lexical, but so far only a few minimal pairs have been found. No grammatical role of tone has been found. The absence of tone marks poses no problems for reading, except in the case of the two words ma, see 2.4 a) geminate consonants and note 2. [fn. 2:] Combining these two morphemes in the orthography is a convention for distinguishing the conditional ma (low tone) from the topic-marker ma (high tone) without introducing accents [i.e. tone diacritics] into the orthography.

new_statements.relation_note: Same picture as the existing statement from Hoskison 1983 (two level lexical tones, H and L; no statement on word stress). The catalog record's rule field is empty; this work supplies no placement rule either, so it confirms the 'tone language, no stress statement' reading rather than adding one. Note this describes the Cameroonian variety (Mayo-Tsanaga), Hoskison the Nigerian one.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Two tonemes, high (acute) and low (grave), shown on short and long vowels; tone is lexical with few minimal pairs and no grammatical function, and it is left unwritten. The document (alphabet, vowels, labialisation/palatalisation prosodies, geminates, glottal stop, ee/oo, tone, word division) says nothing about word stress, accent or prominence; the word 'accents' in footnote 2 refers to tone diacritics, not stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Menetrey & Perrin 2006 describes Gude as spoken in the departement du Mayo-Tsanaga, province de l'Extreme-Nord, Cameroon (title decoded from the custom font: 'Presentation de l'orthographe du Gude'; the SIL landing page titles it 'Présentation de l'orthographe du Guɗe'). Hoskison's works describe the Nigerian side (Mubi area). Both are the same language gude1246.

sources.quote: Hoskison's MA thesis built on his earlier paper 'Prosodies and Verb Stems in Gude' (Hoskison 1974) and was later incorporated into his doctoral dissertation ... In contrast to Mohrlang's analysis of the typologically related Higi (Mohrlang 1972), Hoskison treated palatalization and labialization as features of consonants in Gude, present as such in the underlying representation. [...] Of particular interest is the palatalization strategy adopted by Gude for marking motion-to-speaker on verbs. sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog bium1280). Tone is set aside by design: Souag's open review (LLA 9(1), 2023, doi:10.4000/lla.6137, read in full) states 'No attempt is made to reconstruct tone (2.6.3).' The OpenAlex/CUP abstract says the analyses cover 'both consonants and vowels' with emphasis on palatalisation and labialisation prosodies; the five chapter summaries on Cambridge Core never mention tone. No Gude-specific tone statement is to be expected; Gude reflexes appear only as lexical data.
